candidates.lcsc: N/A - copper, not an LCSC part
candidates.fit: L_s primary pick. Wheeler-formula L=189.7nH, skin-depth ESR gives Q~130-150 (1.3-1.5x proximity derate), P~6.8-7.9W - matches the frozen Q=150/6.7W budget. Zero BOM cost, JLC-native, trimmable at bring-up. Real Q depends on an L2 ground-plane keepout under the coil (P4/P5 layout decision, not yet made) and needs bench confirmation.

L_s Plan-B fallback, unverified: N=4 in parallel (680nH units -> ~170nH total). 15A/5.5mOhm DCR gives huge current margin, but 20MHz Q is NOT published by this vendor family (Sunltech, molded shielded inductor). Paralleling divides current/heat but does NOT raise Q (Q_total=Q_unit for identical parallel units) - do not trust without a bench VNA measurement first.

L_s Plan-B fallback, unverified: N=4 in parallel (680nH units -> ~170nH total). Sunlord's own MWSA-S catalog specs inductance ONLY at 100kHz - no Q, ESR, or SRF at any frequency near 20MHz anywhere in the datasheet. Same bench-verification caveat as the Sunltech pick.

L_s Plan-B fallback, WORST-CASE-KNOWN: the one family with a real vendor Q-vs-frequency chart (read for the datasheet's smaller values). Vishay's own Features line states 'Frequency range up to 5.0 MHz' - 4x below our 20MHz operating point. Reading the chart past that stated range gives Q~20-40 at 20MHz, i.e. P~25-50W in a single 184nH-equivalent part - this is the concrete evidence that catalog molded/shielded inductors are the wrong technology class here, not just an unverified guess.

NOT usable, listed for completeness: genuine high-Q RF wire-wound inductor (Q=25min @100MHz per Murata's real spec, SRF=1300MHz), i.e. the right frequency class - but rated only 140mA vs the 6.6A needed, a 47x shortfall before even considering paralleling ~50 units. Confirms the fundamental current-vs-Q split in this part space: nothing on LCSC has both.

C_s primary pick: 8x in parallel = 448pF (0.2% off the 447pF target). C0G/NP0, 1kV rating (4.6x margin over ~215Vpk peak). Loss is tanD-limited (~0.77-1.16W total for the whole bank regardless of split count); 8-way split keeps each part at ~0.825A rms / ~145mW, comfortable for a 1206. Also doubles as the C_shunt building block (see below) for BOM commonality.

C_s alt: 2x in parallel = 440pF (1.6% off target). Cheaper per part and fewer parts, but each carries ~3.3A rms / ~580mW - likely too much self-heating for an 0805 body; prefer the 8x56pF/1206 pick unless board area is tighter than thermal margin.
C_s alt: 470pF/630V single-value option if fewer BOM lines are preferred over even current-splitting; stock is thinner (437pcs) than the primary pick.

C_shunt primary pick (same part as C_s): 4x in parallel = 224pF (12% over the 200pF external nominal - acceptable, gets tuned against actual Coss tolerance anyway). Exact current/parallel-count needs P2's switched-drain simulation to firm up; this is a reasonable planning default, not a verified final value.
C_shunt alt: single 220pF part at 2kV rating - huge voltage margin if drain-node ringing exceeds the nominal ~215Vpk estimate. Very deep stock (105k).
